recommendation: Keep the empty audit commit as-is. No further core source work is needed for FHIR-7362 unless a future work-group decision reopens lifecycle state terminology more broadly.
issue_request: FHIR-7362 was a Published/Persuasive DSTU1 MnM change request for the FHIR-core lifecycle page. It asked to expand the clinical workflow process lifecycle wording by saying the characteristic state list is non-exhaustive, with comments seeking clearer and more consistent meanings for states such as cancelled versus aborted/stopped. The recorded resolution was to add the proposed words.
initial_application: The issue was applied in SVN revision 6030, mirrored as git commit 7bcfd947d8be1c97bfdfedd0d282c478212e4359, which changed source/lifecycle.html to say "A characteristic (but non-exhaustive) set of states" on the lifecycle page. The current source preserves that accepted wording on the Clinical Workflow Process Life Cycle section.
additional_context: source/lifecycle.html is an active built narrative page because publish.ini lists lifecycle.html for publication. Later source cleanup converted the page from "pattern" terminology to "life cycle" terminology, and the already-published combined-branch FHIR-7363 reconciliation completed one remaining related wording cleanup. Current source also distinguishes cancelled as a planned activity that did not start from stopped/aborted as an activity that began but was not completed. Jira, Zulip, and Confluence searches found no later decision or community discussion requiring a different source change for FHIR-7362.
reconciliation: Made no source change. The current active lifecycle page already contains the non-exhaustive wording requested by FHIR-7362 and already provides the cancelled/stopped distinction the issue comment was concerned about, so further edits would be redundant.
